exposure: Teenage pregnancy (maternal age between 14 and 19 years)
outcome: Obstetric complications (e.g., pregnancy-induced hypertension, hypothyroidism, fetal growth restriction, oligohydramnios)
cohort: 133 adolescent mothers (age 14-19 years) attending antenatal clinic or delivery wards
finding: Teenage pregnancy in this study population was associated with risk factors like early marriage, family pressure, school dropout, and resulted in increased risk of obstetric complications like pregnancy-induced hypertension, and low postpartum contraception acceptance.
